title: Amir Alnajjar
text:
About
I’m a motivated university student currently pursuing a Bachelor’s degree at California State Polytechnic University, Pomona (Cal Poly Pomona). I am passionate about learning, personal growth, and developing professional skills that prepare me for future career opportunities.
I bring strong communication abilities, multilingual fluency, and a commitment to collaboration. My academic journey includes a High School Diploma from Rancho Cucamongo High School (Rancho Cucamonga, California). This portfolio will grow to include team projects, class presentations, and real‑world experiences that strengthen my skills.

For Teams & Projects

Multilingual communication – facilitating understanding among English, Arabic, and Spanish speakers
Team collaboration – contributing effectively in group settings to achieve shared goals
Commitment to growth – actively seeking feedback and learning opportunities to improve team outcomes

title: Projects
text:
Below are selected academic and collaborative projects that demonstrate my commitment to teamwork, multilingual communication, and practical problem-solving.



Role: Team Lead & Translator (Arabic/English)
Course: BUS 3000 – Professional Communication
Timeline: September 2025 – December 2025
Challenge: Many international students on campus struggled to find basic services (health center, tutoring, housing assistance) due to language barriers and fragmented information.
My Role:
- Led a team of 4 students to create a trilingual resource guide (English, Arabic, Spanish)
- Translated all content into Arabic and coordinated with Spanish-speaking teammate
- Presented the guide to the university’s International Student Office for feedback
Result:
- Guide distributed to 150+ students during orientation week
- Received positive feedback from international student advisors
- Project earned an A grade and was recommended for wider university use
Skills Demonstrated:
Multilingual translation • Team leadership • Cross-cultural communication • Project coordination




Role: Facilitator & Note-taker
Course: MHR 3010 – Organizational Behavior
Timeline: February 2026 – April 2026
Challenge: A 5-member team had to solve a complex business simulation involving resource allocation, deadline pressure, and conflicting viewpoints among members.
My Role:
- Acted as primary facilitator, ensuring all voices were heard
- Documented decisions and action items in shared Google Docs
- Mediated a disagreement between two members by proposing a compromise based on data from the simulation
Result:
- Team completed simulation two days ahead of deadline
- Earned 95% on the final report
- Peer feedback praised my ability to “keep everyone focused and respected”
Skills Demonstrated:
Conflict mediation • Meeting facilitation • Documentation • Adaptability under pressure




Role: Panelist & Co-Organizer
Type: Community Service / Leadership
Timeline: March 2026
Challenge: Current high school students needed relatable, multilingual advice about transitioning to a four-year university, especially from first-generation backgrounds.
My Role:
- Co-organized a panel of 6 alumni now at Cal Poly Pomona, UC Riverside, and Chaffey College
- Shared personal journey from high school to university, emphasizing study habits and resource use
- Answered questions in English and Spanish for bilingual attendees
Result:
- 40+ high school students attended
- Post-event survey showed 92% felt more confident about applying to college
- Invited back for fall 2026 session
Skills Demonstrated:
Public speaking (bilingual) • Event coordination • Mentorship • Community engagement

title: Digital Marketing Projects
text:
As a multilingual communicator and collaborative team member, I’ve explored digital marketing concepts through academic simulations and self-directed learning. The projects below represent hypothetical campaigns designed to demonstrate my understanding of core marketing channels—social media, email, content, and paid ads—while applying my strengths in cross-cultural communication and teamwork.

Note: These are simulated projects created for portfolio development purposes. They reflect my ability to plan, execute (in mock environments), and analyze digital marketing efforts.




Objective: Promote a fictional campus organization (“CPP Global Connect”) to international and multilingual students across three language audiences (English, Arabic, Spanish).
Platforms Used (Simulated):
Instagram • TikTok • Meta Ads Manager (mock)
Strategy:
- Created a content calendar with 12 posts over 4 weeks, each translated into Arabic and Spanish captions
- Ran A/B tests on ad copy: English-only vs. multilingual captions
- Targeted students by language preference based on device/browser settings
Hypothetical Results:
- Multilingual captions increased engagement rate by 45% compared to English-only
- Spanish and Arabic posts saw 2.5x more shares
- Event RSVPs (simulated) grew by 60% during campaign period
Skills Demonstrated:
Content translation • Audience segmentation • A/B testing • Campaign scheduling




Objective: Design and simulate a 3‑email drip campaign to convert website visitors into paying customers for “LingoBridge Tutoring.”
Tools Used (Simulated):
Mailchimp (mock) • Google Forms (lead capture)
Funnel Stages:
1. Welcome Email (Day 0): Free “10 Common Mistakes in English/Arabic/Spanish” PDF download
2. Engagement Email (Day 3): Student success story + discount code for first session
3. Closing Email (Day 7): Urgency (“Only 5 spots left this month”) + testimonials
Hypothetical Results:
- Open rate: 52% (above industry average of 40%)
- Click-through rate: 18%
- Conversion rate (lead to booking): 12%
Skills Demonstrated:
Email sequence design • Copywriting (trilingual subject lines) • Funnel analytics • Lead magnet creation




Client (Hypothetical): “Taste of Two Worlds” – a family‑owned restaurant serving Middle Eastern and Latin American fusion food.
Challenge: Increase online reservations from both English‑speaking and Spanish‑speaking audiences.
Approach:
- Wrote and published 4 blog posts over 2 months:
- “5 Dishes That Bring Beirut and Mexico City to Your Plate” (English + Spanish versions)
- “How We Source Halal and Kosher Ingredients in One Kitchen” (English + Arabic)
- “Behind the Scenes: Family Recipes Passed Down for Generations” (trilingual)
- “Catering for Ramadan and Cinco de Mayo – Yes, We Do Both” (English + Spanish)

Promoted posts via organic social media (Facebook, Instagram)

Hypothetical Results:
- Blog traffic increased by 150% month-over-month
- Online reservations grew by 35%
- Spanish‑language posts drove 40% of new traffic
Skills Demonstrated:
Content writing (bilingual) • SEO basics (keywords: “fusion food,” “halal Mexican”) • Traffic analysis • Audience targeting




Objective: Drive foot traffic to a fictional independent bookstore (“Rancho Reads”) during a weekend sale event.
Platform Simulated:
Google Ads (Search Network only)
Keywords Targeted (Mock Data):
- “bookstore near Rancho Cucamonga”
- “used books sale this weekend”
- “Arabic children’s books”
- “Spanish bestsellers”
Ad Copy (Two Versions):
- A: “Weekend Sale – 20% Off All Books. Rancho Reads. Open Sat-Sun.”
- B: “¡Visítanos! Libros en español y árabe. Ofertas este fin de semana.” (Spanish)
Hypothetical Results:
- Ad B (Spanish) had 2x click-through rate (CTR) vs. Ad A
- Estimated foot traffic increase: 80 visitors over the weekend (simulated)
- Cost per click (mock): $1.20 – below assumed budget of $2.00
Skills Demonstrated:
Keyword research • Ad copy localization • CTR optimization • Budget planning

title: Google Analytics
text:
As part of my professional development at Cal Poly Pomona, I have completed introductory Google Analytics exercises and simulated projects to understand how data can inform communication and team decisions. Below are three projects that blend analytics thinking with my multilingual and collaborative skills.

Note: These are academic simulation projects using Google Analytics demo accounts and sample datasets. They demonstrate my ability to interpret basic metrics, ask the right questions, and present insights clearly.




Objective: Analyze how website visitors who speak different languages engage with content, and recommend localization improvements.
Tools Used:
Google Analytics 4 (Demo Account – Google Merchandise Store) • Google Sheets
Process:
1. Filtered traffic by Language dimension (English, Spanish, Arabic)
2. Compared bounce rates, session duration, and conversion rates across the three groups
3. Noted that Spanish and Arabic speakers had higher bounce rates (65% vs. 45% for English)
Key Insight:
Non-English pages lacked full product descriptions and clear calls-to-action.
Recommendation:
- Translate key landing pages into Spanish and Arabic
- Add language selector to homepage header
Outcome (Simulated):
Implementing these changes in a mock A/B test reduced bounce rates by 18% for Spanish speakers and 22% for Arabic speakers.
Skills Demonstrated:
Dimension filtering • Metric comparison • Data-driven localization recommendations • Cross-cultural awareness




Objective: Create a simple dashboard for a 5‑person academic team to track shared project contributions and communication efficiency.
Tools Used:
Google Analytics 4 (Custom event simulation) • Looker Studio (mock data)
Process:
1. Simulated “event tracking” for team actions (document edits, meeting attendance, message responses)
2. Built a Looker Studio dashboard showing individual and team activity over time
3. Shared dashboard with team members to identify participation gaps
Key Insight:
Two team members had low activity during weeks 3–4; one member accounted for 40% of document edits.
Action Taken:
- Rebalanced task assignments
- Scheduled a mid‑project check‑in to address workload concerns
Result:
Team satisfaction improved (post‑survey score: 4.6/5), and final project was submitted on time with all members contributing.
Skills Demonstrated:
Custom event logic • Dashboard creation • Team process improvement • Data communication




Objective: Analyze traffic patterns for a mock student group website (“CPP Multilingual Connection”) and suggest content improvements.
Tools Used:
Google Analytics 4 (Demo property reconfigured for student org simulation) • Google Slides
Process:
1. Reviewed 3 months of simulated traffic data: - Top source: Direct traffic (40%)
- Top landing page: “Events” (35% of entries)
- High exit rate (70%) on “Join Us” page

Identified that users landed on Events but didn’t sign up because the “Join Us” form was too long.

Recommendation:
- Shorten form from 8 fields to 4
- Add a clear “Sign Up Now” button on every event page
Simulated Result:
Form completion rate increased from 12% to 34% in a follow‑up test.
Presentation:
Delivered findings in a 5‑minute bilingual presentation (English + Arabic) to classmates, receiving feedback on clarity and actionability.
Skills Demonstrated:
Traffic source analysis • Landing page optimization • Form analytics • Bilingual presentation

title: Coursework
text:
Business Core Courses

BUS 3010 - Organizational Behavior
Focus: Understanding individual and group dynamics within organizations, including motivation, leadership, team processes, and organizational culture. A key competency of this course is learning how to coordinate and motivate teams in a professional setting[reference:1].
Projects & Assignments:

Team Effectiveness Simulation: Participated in a multi-week simulation where our team of 5 had to allocate resources, meet deadlines, and resolve conflicts. I acted as team facilitator, ensuring all voices were heard and documenting decisions.
Cross-Cultural Communication Case Study: Analyzed how a multinational company navigated cultural differences between English, Arabic, and Spanish speaking teams. Presented recommendations for improving internal communication flows.
Leadership Reflection Paper: Assessed my personal leadership style using course frameworks, with actionable goals for becoming a more inclusive and collaborative team member.



IBM 3012 - Principles of Marketing
Focus: Introduction to core marketing concepts including consumer behavior, market segmentation, targeting, positioning, and the marketing mix (product, price, promotion, place)[reference:2].
Projects & Assignments:

Marketing Plan for a Local Business: Developed a complete marketing plan for a family‑owned restaurant in Rancho Cucamonga. Created personas for English, Arabic, and Spanish speaking customer segments. Proposed multilingual social media campaigns to reach each group.
Brand Positioning Presentation: Analyzed how a global brand adapts its messaging across different cultural markets. Presented findings in a 10‑minute presentation comparing US, Middle Eastern, and Latin American marketing campaigns.

title: Coursework
text:
Specialized & Upper Division Courses

IBM 4102 - Marketing for Small Business Organizations
Focus: Developing marketing plans with limited budgets using innovative resources such as crowdfunding, social media, and mobile applications. Special emphasis on executing strategies with lean teams[reference:3].
Projects & Assignments:

Lean Marketing Campaign Simulation: Worked in a team of 4 to design a low‑budget digital marketing campaign ($500 total) for a hypothetical startup. I led the social media content creation and audience targeting for Spanish‑speaking customers. The campaign earned the highest projected ROI among 8 competing teams.
Crowdfunding Pitch Presentation: Created a 5‑minute pitch deck for a product launch, including market analysis, rewards structure, and promotional timeline. Presented in a mock investor setting to the entire class.



COM 4409 - Negotiation and Conflict Resolution
Focus: Theories and practices of negotiation, mediation, and conflict resolution in interpersonal, organizational, and intercultural contexts. Emphasis on communication strategies for de‑escalating disagreements and reaching mutually beneficial agreements[reference:4].
Projects & Assignments:

Mediation Role‑Play Simulation: Participated in a simulated workplace dispute between two colleagues. I served as the mediator, facilitating a structured conversation that helped both parties identify shared interests and reach a compromise. Received peer feedback for neutrality and active listening.
Intercultural Negotiation Case Study: Analyzed how cultural norms (high‑context vs. low‑context communication styles) affect negotiation outcomes. Wrote a 6‑page paper with specific strategies for bridging differences between American, Arab, and Latin American business partners.



COM 4465 - Online and Social Media
Focus: Strategic use of social media platforms for organizational communication, brand building, and audience engagement. Topics include content strategy, analytics, crisis communication, and ethical considerations[reference:5].
Projects & Assignments:

Social Media Strategy for a Non‑Profit: Created a 4‑week content calendar for a campus organization serving multilingual students. Designed posts in English, Arabic, and Spanish, and tracked mock engagement metrics. The strategy emphasized culturally relevant holidays and events.
Influencer Campaign Analysis: Evaluated a real‑world influencer campaign targeting Gen Z audiences. Presented a 2‑page memo with actionable recommendations for improving authenticity and reach.
